blocks.md: This lesson follows **The Minimal Intervention Principle and Optimization Filters** in *Safety Enforcement* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Safety Enforcement, § The Minimal Intervention Principle and Optimization Filters
blocks.md: When the arm approaches the cage-door latch too quickly while still proposing a useful target and direction, rejecting every such proposal would discard useful learned behavior, whereas accepting it unchecked would exceed the permitted approach speed. The **minimal intervention principle** resolves this trade-off by passing an admissible proposal untouched and choosing the smallest feasible correction, one that satisfies physical constraints and finishes before the permission deadline, whenever a proposal crosses a boundary. The resulting **safety shield** preserves useful task progress within the physical limits.

questions.q: The section **The Minimal Intervention Principle and Optimization Filters** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A barrier guarantee holds only under model fidelity, bounded disturbance, actuation within a qualified effort error and delay, solver completion inside its budget, and a sample period short enough for inter-sample drift, each watched at runtime.
Available deceleration is net of gravity and bias in the worst direction, and integrator unwinding and saturation spend it before the stop begins.
When contact is the task the kinetic barrier admits only zero speed, so an energy-tank passivity barrier and a separately qualified force channel replace clearance as the margin.
The pedestrian intrusion distance v_h(tau + T_stop) sets how much clearance a walking person consumes during the stop, which bounds the walking-person speed ceiling.
